violation_type.title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §742.303(2))
violation_type.short_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control
violation_type.typical_finding: It has been determined through interviews, that the older children in care did change diapers of the younger children and had clean up duties.

finding_variants.text: It has been determined through interviews, that the older children in care did change diapers of the younger children and had clean up duties.

During the course of the investigation, it was determined that the caregiver did not use good judgment when she did not release the children to the designated release person.  The caregiver also did not use good judgment when she shared information with the children about their father that was not appropriate.
The primary caregiver did not use good judgement when she allowed the children to be cared for in a home that was not permitted, and the person did not have a background check.
Based on the DFPS investigation, the caregiver did not use good judgement as a child was placed in a restricted device for approximately 20-30 minutes.

Based on the evidence obtained during the DFPS investigation, the primary caregiver used poor judgement when the children in care were left under the supervision of someone who did not meet substitute caregiver qualifications. Additionally, substitute caregiver was unable to intervene physically or verbally prior to a child running away from the home.
